narr: A slow moving low pressure system, along with plenty of moisture, allowed for showers and thunderstorms to gradually move through the Ohio Valley during the day on May 6th. Heavy rainfall occurred with these storms and additional storm and shower activity developed over the same areas, leading to flash flooding. A few roads throughout southeast Ohio were affected by flooding, one of which in Lawrence County was impassable for a time. Even after the rain had passed, several creeks and rivers rose above their bankfull and flood stage for the next two days, which resulted in minor flooding for areas adjacent to the water.
ev: Route 93 was closed due to flooding around Mile Marker 10 near the city of Lisman.
High water flowed over Lick Run Road which also led to some minor debris on the roadway.
lsr: COUNTY DISPATCH REPORTS THAT ROUTE 93 WAS CLOSED AT MILE MARKER 10 DUE TO FLOODING FROM HEAVY RAIN TONIGHT.
SHERIFF OFFICE REPORTS THAT LICK RUN ROAD HAD FLOWING WATER ACROSS IT WITH SOME MINOR DEBRIS ALSO ON THE ROADWAY.
